sections.title: What this module covers
sections.body: Rails views are deliberately thin — the business logic lives in models and services, the view just presents it. This page covers the view layer topics that appear in intermediate interviews: layout inheritance and content_for/yield, partials with locals (and the performance difference between render collection: vs looping), form_with and how it generates CSRF tokens, the security risk of html_safe and raw, helper methods vs decorators vs ViewComponent, and the asset pipeline evolution (Sprockets → Webpacker → importmap). The XSS question hides in the view layer — 'when does Rails escape HTML and when doesn't it?' — and the answer requires knowing that ERB auto-escapes via <%= %> but raw and html_safe bypass that protection.

sections.title: Key topics and depth markers
sections.body: Topics: layouts-partials, form-helpers, view-components, asset-pipeline. Each topic has dedicated Q&A covering the concept, the comparison, the internal mechanics, and the scenario-based questions interviewers use to test production understanding.

sections.title: How interviewers probe this module
sections.body: Interviewers at Rails-focused companies probe these topics by opening with a definition question, then immediately following up with when would you use X vs Y? and what are the gotchas?. The depth marker is always the trade-off and the failure mode — not just the API surface.
